_comment: Real Bonjour strings, committed so the naming rules are tested against what the
network actually says rather than against what this code expects it to say.
Provenance is recorded per entry. 'spec' entries are the strings recorded in
SPEC.md section 6, captured from the reference network during earlier work.
'captured' entries were read off 10.10.20.0/24 with `dns-sd -B` on 2026-09-03
while building this phase. 'constructed' entries are shapes the rules must handle
that no device on this network produces — they are labelled so nobody mistakes

Entries marked 'constructed (unicode)' pin a crash rather than a naming rule: lowercased() does not preserve length for these scalars, and computing a range against a lowered copy then slicing the original trapped on them.

instance_names.note: Fullname form: a hardware-address prefix AND a service suffix, both cut.
Instance-label form, as a browse reply delivers it.
The same device as the _companion-link entry below, named differently.
Already clean. The rules must leave it alone.
Non-ASCII apostrophe U+2019, which must survive intact through to the JSON.
avahi appends the MAC so two hosts with one name do not collide.
A bracketed suffix that is NOT a MAC must be kept. The rule parses, it does not pattern-match.
An at-sign in an ordinary name. A loose 'everything before the @' rule would truncate this.
A prefix and nothing else is not a name. Must be rejected, not returned empty.
U+0130 LATIN CAPITAL I WITH DOT ABOVE lowercases to TWO scalars. A range from a lowered copy indexes past the end of the original and traps.
U+212A KELVIN SIGN lowercases to 'k', which encodes shorter. Same defect, opposite direction.
U+1E9E LATIN CAPITAL SHARP S lowercases to U+00DF.
Precomposed A-ring, plus a non-ASCII name that must survive intact.
No suffix at all, so the rule must return the name untouched rather than mis-slicing it.

txt_models.note: THE TRAP. `md` on _raop is the supported-metadata list, not a model. Reading it fills the report with "0,1,2".
With `md` alone there is no model at all, and the honest answer is nothing.
First NON-EMPTY wins. An empty `am` must not shadow a later key.
Publishers are inconsistent about case. `MD` must be forbidden as firmly as `md`.
md IS the model here. Forbidding it globally to dodge the _raop trap silently discarded the real model on every Chromecast, Nest and Android TV.
Case-insensitively, and still permitted: the exclusion is scoped to a service type, not to a spelling.
Any type that is not _raop reads md normally.
And on _raop it is still refused, with nothing to fall back to.
